Singapore construction costs may stay elevated and rise by a further 2.3% to 3.3% in 2027: JLL
article:
Geopolitical volatility, supply chain vulnerability and surging demand for AI-driven technical facilities could keep Singapore’s construction cost environment “challenging” over the next 12 months, in JLL’s view.

The real estate consultancy is forecasting construction costs in the city-state to rise by 2.5% to 3.5% for the whole of this year, before easing slightly to an increase of 2.3% to 3.3% in 2027.

“The outlook is supported by a balanced pipeline of Build-To-Order (BTO) public housing, mixed-use commercial and infrastructure works,” JLL said on Nov 11 as it released its Global Construction Costs Index 2026 report.

This comes as Asia Pacific’s (Apac) construction costs are moving up at a similar pace to North America and more quickly than Europe. The firm expects Apac’s cost growth to come in at around 3.8% to 4.7% next year.

Cost pressures in this region stem from a mix of factors, including geopolitical disruption to energy and material supply chains, acute shortages of skilled labour, land scarcity in key gateway cities such as Hong Kong and Singapore, as well as a spike in demand for specialised construction driven by data-centre and advanced-manufacturing expansion.

Real estate developers will need to adopt more agile risk and supply chain management to keep projects on course, if they do not want to fall behind, suggested Daniel Malacchini, JLL’s head of cost advisory and cost management, project and development services, Apac.

In particular, Apac’s dependence on Middle Eastern energy supplies and construction materials — combined with longer, more complex supply chains — has amplified cost pressures.

Singapore, for one, illustrates how exposed import-dependent markets are to such swings.

Base materials costs went up by 7.4% in the first half of 2026, compared to the 2025 average. Steel has been more volatile, falling 1.45% in the first half of this year before a 10.3% rebound is forecast for the second half.

“Energy price volatility, transportation disruption and base materials costs all feed directly into regional tender prices,” said Shweta Choudhari, director, work dynamics research, Asia Pacific, JLL.

She added that contractors are increasingly pricing in geopolitical uncertainty as a permanent risk premium rather than a temporary measure.

Although Singapore’s forecast cost increase is below the regional pace, cumulative tender price inflation since 2021 in the city-state has reached 30.2% — surpassing consumer price inflation of 17.7%.

This gap, of more than 12 percentage points, is the highest in Apac alongside Australia, according to JLL.

With construction cost inflation outpacing consumer inflation in major Apac economies, it is “creating a disconnect between broader economic indicators and development feasibility realities”, the firm wrote.

Developers relying on Consumer Price Index (CPI)-based escalation assumptions may therefore be underestimating actual cost growth, which could lead to mid-project re-underwriting and threaten returns.

title: JTC Tuas B2 factory with unused plot ratio offered for sale with $13.8 mil price tag
article:
A Business 2 (B2) factory at 8 Tuas Avenue 10 has been put on the market with a guide price of $13.8 million, via an expression of interest (EOI) exercise.

That works out to about $222 psf on the regular-shaped land plot of about 62,026 sq ft.

Based on the existing gross floor area (GFA) of about 50,553 sq ft, the guide price translates to $273 psf.

There is potential to increase the GFA to around 86,835 sq ft, subject to the approval of JTC and the relevant authorities, said marketing agent Huttons.

This is because the site is currently built to a plot ratio of about 0.82 — well below the permissible plot ratio of 1.4, the firm added. Going by the maximum potential GFA, the price tag is about $159 psf.

Aric Lim, group district director at Huttons, said that the property’s unused plot ratio sets it apart.

“An owner-occupier can run operations from day one, and expand on the same site later, rather than relocating as the business grows,” he added.

JTC has granted a lease extension for the site till Dec 31, 2054.

Such JTC factories in the west with a remaining lease of about 28 years are “not easy to come by”, especially one with a regular plot of over 60,000 sq ft, Lim noted.

Quek Fujin, head of business space at Huttons, expects interest from industrial business users looking to consolidate, investors seeking a long-lease industrial asset with rental upside, and developers who wish to redevelop it and maximise the GFA.

Located within Tuas, the factory is accessible via the Ayer Rajah Expressway, Pioneer Road and the Tuas West Road MRT Station.

It is also near Tuas Mega Port, which is being developed into the world’s largest fully automated container terminal, and close to the Malaysia-Singapore Second Link connecting to Johor.

Owing to its location, the property is “optimised for efficient logistics and industrial operations”, said Lee Sze Teck, senior director of data analytics at Huttons.

As the property is on JTC land, the sale will be subject to JTC’s approval of the buyer and its intended use.

Viewings by interested parties are strictly by appointment. The EOI closes on Dec 15.

title: Twelve luxury units at Martin Modern, Wallich Residence linked to $3 bil laundering case head to auction
article:
Twelve apartments at Martin Modern in River Valley and Wallich Residence in Tanjong Pagar, linked to Singapore’s $3 billion money laundering case, will go under the hammer at Singapore Realtors Inc (SRI)’s auction on Nov 25.

Seven two-bedroom units at Martin Modern are on offer at a guide price of $2.238 million each, or $2,929 psf. Five three-bedroom units at Wallich Residence carry a guide price of $4.42 million each, or $3,366 psf.

The auction follows sales at SRI’s two previous auctions. In September, SRI sold four units, two each at Wallich Residence and Martin Modern, says Mok Sze Sze, managing partner of SRI Auction. A unit at New Futura was then sold at the October auction.

“The encouraging results across successive auctions reflect the continued presence of buyer interest in quality luxury residential properties within the Core Central Region segment,” adds Mok.

Higher-floor units at both projects drew multiple bids at the September auction, particularly from buyers who value views, privacy and exclusivity, Mok notes. The November auction will again feature higher-floor units.

The Martin Modern units, on Levels 25 to 28, are about 764 sq ft each. The 450-unit, twin 30-storey condo at 8 Martin Place in District 9 has a 99-year lease from 2016. Facilities include a swimming pool, gym, and barbecue pavilion.

It is within walking distance of Great World MRT Station on the Thomson-East Coast Line and Great World mall, with easy access to Orchard Road and Marina Bay.

River Valley Primary School is within 1km, while Alexandra Primary School, Anglo-Chinese School (Junior), Cantonment Primary School, St Margaret’s School (Primary) and Zhangde Primary School are within 1km to 2km.

The Wallich Residence units, of about 1,313 sq ft each, are on levels 46, 47, 49 and 50 of Guoco Tower . At 290m and 64 storeys, it is currently Singapore’s tallest building.

The tower’s 181 apartments occupy levels 39 to 64, above 38 storeys of Grade A office space. The wider integrated development includes a six-storey retail podium of about 100,000 sq ft, linked to Tanjong Pagar MRT station via the basement, and the 223-room Sofitel Singapore City Centre.

Residents can use facilities such as a swimming pool, sky garden and concierge services. Beyond the retail podium, they are within walking distance of 100 AM , International Plaza and Tanjong Pagar Plaza .

All units are sold with vacant possession. The auction will be held at 2.30pm on Nov 25 at SRI’s office at Great World West Tower.

title: Hot demand for BTO flats in November 2026 launch amid new income ceilings, more SWT homes
article:
The latest Build-To-Order (BTO) sales exercise saw a sharp rise in applications, with robust demand across all categories, including community care apartments (CCAs), two-room flexi flats, as well as three-room and bigger flat types.

As at 5pm on Nov 11, the overall application rate was 4.5, with 35,603 prospective buyers vying for the 7,964 available flats. Applications will close at 11.59pm on Nov 11.

The current application rate already exceeds the 3.4 recorded in June 2026’s exercise, and is also the highest since August 2022.

The total number of applicants also climbed by about 46%, from 23,894 back in June, and is the highest since October 2024.

The November 2026 round offered 7,964 BTO flats across seven projects in Sembawang, Tengah, Yishun, Bedok, Geylang and Toa Payoh.

The most popular projects, drawing the biggest applicant turnouts, were Toa Payoh Hillside, Bayshore Sails and Bayshore Oasis .

First-timer competition was also the steepest for four-room flats at Toa Payoh Hillside and two-room flexi units at Plantation Dew.

Christine Sun, chief researcher and strategist of Realion (OrangeTee & ETC) Group, said the strong overall application rate could be driven by the increased income ceiling, more flats with shorter waiting times (SWT), and more projects in attractive locations.

Likewise, Eugene Lim, ERA Singapore’s key executive officer, noted that this is the first BTO exercise under the new income ceilings of $16,000 for families and $8,000 for singles.

“November’s launch has opened the door for higher-earning households to pursue homes in choice locations,” Lim added. “More buyers were willing to come forward in November, as the strong slate of BTO projects and revised income ceilings provided greater incentive to apply.”

Toa Payoh and Bayshore shine

Prime project Toa Payoh Hillside saw the hottest demand overall despite having the highest clawback rate, attracting almost 6,000 applicants and a 6.6 application rate among first-time families for four-room flats.

Sun attributed the interest in Toa Payoh Hillside to buyers’ confidence “that its prime location will draw healthy capital returns, and that future resale prices may be high enough to offset the recovery amount”.

Moreover, the project is next to Caldecott MRT Station and close to schools such as CHIJ Primary and Secondary, with ample amenities in Toa Payoh.

The next most popular were Bayshore Sails and Bayshore Oasis, both Plus projects, which collectively drew more than 5,000 applicants with an application rate of 3.0.

“The high number of applicants for both sites is in line with our earlier prediction,” said Sun.

Lim noted that the return of Bayshore as a BTO location likely helped sustain interest, as the area has not seen any new flat supply since Bayshore Vista and Bayshore Palms were launched in October 2024.

“This marks the first time in two years that buyers have had the opportunity to secure a home near East Coast Park with direct access to Bayshore MRT station,” he said.

Tengah: Maturing estate with lower entry prices

Over in Tengah in the west, two-room flexi units at Plantation Dew drew a healthy response, with 17.9 first-timer singles applying per available unit (as at 12pm).

This suggests that demand is not confined to centrally located or established estates, noted SRI head of research and data analytics, Mohan Sandrasegeran.

It could also reflect Tengah’s ongoing transformation from a newly developing estate, as it is “no longer simply a future residential town taking shape, but one where more residents are progressively moving into their completed homes”, he shared.

Amenities such as Plantation Plaza and Parc Point are also being introduced in the town, while the upcoming Jurong Region Line and the planned relocation of Anglo-Chinese School (Primary) to Tengah in 2030 could have made it even more attractive to homebuyers, in Sandrasegeran’s view.

Meanwhile, ERA’s Lim said the strong response to Plantation Dew may also be due to pent-up BTO demand in Tengah, which has not seen any HDB launches since Plantation Edge I and II in October 2023.

“Factoring in grants, prices for two-room Flexi flats at Plantation Dew start at $11,000,” Lim noted.

“This is significantly lower than the previous $34,000 starting price (including grants) for two-room Flexi flats at Plantation Edge I & II, as well as nearby resale prices of $322,500 to $388,000, offering buyers a much lower entry point into Tengah.”

Sembawang draws muted turnout

On the other hand, the least popular was Sembawang Anchor, a Standard project, with a subdued turnout.

Four- and five-room flats in Sembawang yielded the lowest application rate of less than 1 among first-timer families, despite having SWT flats.

Huttons CEO Mark Yip reckoned that the project’s location, which is farther away from an MRT station, contributed to the anaemic demand even with the shorter construction period.

“The long distance from an MRT station is still a big minus for applicants,” Yip added.

ERA’s Lim said: “While overall demand for Sembawang Anchor was muted, the quieter response offers a clear advantage to serious applicants seeking flats with shorter waiting times.”

With first-timer family subscription rates for three-room and larger units ranging from 0.3 to 1.0 at Sembawang Anchor (as at 12pm), most applicants would be able to secure a home, he added.

Sun of Realion said the muted demand in Sembawang was within expectations because there is an ample supply of new flats in the area, with a total of almost 4,000 units launched in both the February and June sales exercises this year.

“Those who intended to stay here would have applied in the past,” she continued.

Keen interest across the board

Applications totalled 494 for community care apartments, 12,670 for two-room flexi flats, and 21,828 for three-room and larger flats as at 3pm on Nov 11.

In particular, the application rate for community care apartments in this launch jumped to 2.0, from less than 1.0 in the last three projects with such homes.

“This was likely due to the lowering in fees for seniors applying for CCAs,” said Yip from Huttons.

The government in July adjusted the basic service package (BSP) for community care apartments to make it more affordable for seniors, with the monthly BSP fees lowered by between 18% and 75%. “The higher take-up shows that the policy change is in the right direction,” Yip added.

Commenting on the overall application rate for the November 2026 exercise, SRI’s Sandrasegeran pointed out that while the revised income ceilings may have resulted in a broader pool of eligible applicants, it would be hard to determine their direct impact without more detailed information on the profile of applicants.

Application demand is also influenced by factors such as project location, pricing, transport accessibility and individual household preferences.

“Nevertheless, the revised income ceilings represent a positive development in broadening access to subsidised public housing,” Sandrasegeran said.

In addition, the November exercise also came after a relatively extended interval since the previous BTO launch in June. That may have contributed to interest from prospective homebuyers who had been waiting for another opportunity to enter the BTO market, he said.

title: Singapore's cold storage logistics market set to grow on food and life sciences demand
article:
Demand for cold storage facilities — climate-controlled spaces needed for storing and distributing temperature-sensitive products — is set to grow in Singapore, according to a research report published by CBRE in November.

The “niche but critical” segment within the industrial real estate market is poised for further growth, backed by growing food needs as well as the growing life sciences industry, the firm says.

The drivers are expected to support occupancy and rents for cold storage assets, the latter of which CBRE is projecting to grow between 2% and 4% annually up to 2029.

Current landscape

Cold storage facilities form part of Singapore’s wider cold chain logistics industry, which cater to domestic movements of goods as well as imports and exports.

Currently, cold storage facilities make up just 10.4 million sq ft, or 7.8%, of Singapore’s warehouse stock, based on CBRE’s estimates. “The market remains fragmented, with most facilities owner-occupied and relatively small in scale,” the report states.

Cold storage assets typically command a rental premium over logistics facilities without temperature-controlled specifications. Leases usually range for three to five years at multi-tenanted cold storage assets, and up to 10 years or more for build-to-suite tenants.

Cold chain logistics rental ranges

The food industry has largely driven the supply of cold storage warehouses in Singapore. Businesses ranging from grocery chains to food manufacturers and distributors use these facilities to process and store perishables including meat, seafood, fruits, vegetables, dairy and grains.

According to CBRE, licensed cold stores in Singapore grew at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 6.6% over the past six years, going from 175 in 2019 to 257 in 2025.

Groth of cold storage and food processing/manufacturing establishments in Singapore

This mirrors the growth of food processing and manufacturing establishments, which rose by a 6.3% CAGR over the same period to 2,655 last year. “Cold storage has kept pace with the food industry it serves, holding close to 10% of licensed food establishments throughout,” the report adds.

Apart from food-related industries, cold stores are also utilised by pharmaceutical companies for medicines and vaccines that need to be stored at specific temperatures.

While the Covid-19 pandemic resulted in a surge of cold storage additions in 2021, lifting growth in facilities to 16.3% y-o-y that year, the boom has since moderated, with growth coming in at 3.6% in 2025.

Positive catalysts

Still, the steady rise in the number of licensed cold stores point to “sustained demand”, says CBRE. The firm expects the cold chain logistics industry to see continued growth, supported by positive catalysts.

These include Singapore’s growing population, which it anticipates to boost demand for F&B products. At the same time, growing affluence is expected to bolster demand for fresh foods such as meat and dairy, which will further drive the need for cold storage requirements.

Data compiled in CBRE’s report indicates Singapore real consumer spending on food is projected to grow by 2.4% annually to hit $14.4 billion by 2034, while the number of supermarkets and hypermarkets in the city are forecasted to exceed 570 by 2030.

Singapore’s emphasis on food resilience will also amplify the importance of cold chain logistics. The city, which imports over 90% of its food, has a food security approach built on four pillars,  — including diversifying imports, stockpiling food supplies and growing food locally — all of which involve cold chain logistics in some capacity.

Meanwhile, Singapore’s position as a leading life sciences hub in Asia Pacific is also contributing to cold chain demand. CBRE estimates temperature-controlled warehouse space for pharmaceutical and life sciences use currently accounts for over 10% of Singapore’s overall cold chain supply.

More biopharmaceutical companies are investing in new production facilities in the city-state. Recent additions include China’s WuXi XDC, which opened its first overseas manufacturing facility in September at Tuas Biomedical Park.

Growing demand for modern facilities

While demand for cold storage facilities continues to build, availability of spaces is an issue, given that much of the future pipeline is reserved for occupiers’ own use, limiting options for third-party users.

CBRE predicts new supply to average at 0.64 million sq ft per annum from 2026 to 2029, 37% higher than the 0.47 million sq ft annual average across the past 10 years (2016 to 2025). “However, single-user sites account for most of it, with the redevelopment of 2 Fishery Port Road by ESR Reit being the only multi-tenanted project in the pipeline,” the report says.

Historical cold chain logistics completions and future supply

The fragmented market is exacerbated by ageing assets. According to CBRE, nearly a third of existing cold storage buildings are over 20 years old, with specifications that are becoming obsolete.

Against this backdrop, a two-tier market is emerging, with occupiers preferring modern facilities that are more energy-efficient and offer greater automation.

Investment appetite

Given its encouraging supply and demand factors, cold storage buildings are a popular alternative investment asset among investors, who are drawn to the segment’s income stability and attractive yields. CBRE’s research finds that storage assets may deliver yields of around 5.5% to 6.5%.

However, acquisition opportunities remain limited, the firm notes. Recent notable transactions listed in its report include the purchase of 15 Senoko Loop, a facility with a gross floor area (GFA) of over 446,000 sq ft that includes a climate-controlled warehouse, by Hines, Mitsubishi Estate and MBK Real Estate for $53.2 million in 2024.

The limited stock could prompt investors to explore other routes into the sector, such as Daiwa Japan’s House’s acquisition of Singapore cold chain logistics business Storbest Holdings in 2023.

“Amalgamating and redeveloping older, fragmented sites presents another route to scale up,” it adds.

title: Smart Thought Of The Week: Cracks
article:
AI has been described as a transformative technology, in much the same way that the internet, the telephone, the industrial revolution, air travel, railways have been transformational. There is little doubt that AI could appreciably change the way that we do things from planning a holiday to writing a report. But how will AI make money?
Sure, AI has shown itself to be quite clever. It has been able to hack into websites, and it has uncovered flaws in software codes. Great. It has beaten a grandmaster at chess, and it has even defeated top-ranked players at the ancient board game Go. But where’s the money in that? Maybe I am missing something here.
Some proponents of AI have said that it is a technology that allows machines to perform tasks that typically require human intelligence. So, AI can learn to reason, recognise speech, interpret images and it could even solve complex math problems. But, again, where’s the money?
Additionally, which AI platform, if any will dominate? Is Claude better than Gemini? Is ChatGPT better than Co-pilot? Who knows?
Some AI agents can even act like personal assistants. But how safe is it to let AI have access to our emails and personal data so that it can execute sensitive actions such as make purchases on our behalf? How many people will sign up and pay for services like that? Some might.
Point is, AI will need to be monetised somehow to justify the investments. But it could take time. And that is the problem for investors. Currently, hyperscalers have spent hundreds of billions of dollars on building the infrastructure that forms the bedrock for AI. But the returns on investment have been disappointing.
Could what we are witnessing be a case of someone building a better mousetrap and hoping that the world will beat a path to AI’s door? But building a better contraption is unlikely to be enough. The improved mousetrap needs to be marketed, which requires a basic understanding of human needs, wants and demands.
It is that last part of consumer behaviour that is crucial. It is the willingness for people to pay for their needs and wants that they don’t yet know they need and want. That could happen, given time. But for now, AI companies are still feeling their way around the new technology.
In the meantime, the picks and shovel makers could be better positioned to capitalise on the AI buildout. It might not be nearly as exciting as picking the next AI winner. But jam today tastes a lot better than dry toast tomorrow.
Admittedly, cracks have started to appear in some AI outfits, following the change of guard in the US. This is unlikely to derail the rollout of AI, though. It might slow it down. But too much has been invested in AI to  stop it. The AI genie is out of the bottle. It will continue to eat its way through the business world one byte at a time until it is fully satiated.

title: 3 Temasek-Linked SGX Stocks Rewarding Investors With Special Dividends
article:
Extra dividends feel like a year-end bonus.
While you should welcome them, you shouldn’t just build your budget around them.
Three SGX-listed names with
Temasek as a major shareholder
are rewarding investors, or plan to, with payouts on top of their usual dividends.
Here is how much of each company Temasek, a global investment company headquartered in Singapore, owns.

A shared shareholder does not mean a shared source of cash.
Each of these companies funds its extra payout from a different pool.
As a
dividend investor
, your job is to look past the extra and ask whether the core business can keep the ordinary payout growing.
Can DBS keep growing its ordinary dividend?
DBS Group Holdings Ltd
(SGX: D05) declared a total dividend of S$0.81 per share for the third quarter of 2026 (3Q2026).
The payout has two parts, and you should look at them separately.
The ordinary dividend came in at S$0.66, up from S$0.60 a year ago.
That works out to a 10% increase.
The capital return dividend stayed at S$0.15.
The ordinary dividend relies on recurring profit, and DBS has plenty of it.
For the first nine months of 2026 (9M2026), the bank reported a record net profit of S$8.8 billion, while return on equity (ROE) stood at 17%.
Lending kept growing too.
Customer loans rose 9.5% year on year (YoY) to S$478.6 billion.
The non-performing loan (NPL) ratio improved from 1.0% to 0.9%.
The latest quarter had soft spots.
Net interest margin narrowed from 1.96% to 1.87% as Singapore interest rates fell.
Markets trading non-interest income dropped to S$17 million from S$419 million.
Net profit for 3Q 2026 fell 4.8% YoY to S$2.8 billion.
For 2027, management expects total income growth in the mid-single-digit range.
The CEO also cautioned that elevated energy prices and geopolitical risks have made the outlook more uncertain.
What is funding Keppel REIT’s extra distributions?
Although
Keppel REIT
(SGX: K71U) did not report a distribution per unit (DPU) for 9M2026, its distributable income provides a better read.
Distributable income from operations grew 24.4% YoY to S$179.9 million.
That figure leaves out a S$15 million Anniversary Distribution.
Once you add it back, distributable income reached S$194.9 million.
A second one-off is on the way.
The REIT will return S$15 million of divestment proceeds to unitholders in three semi-annual tranches from the second half of 2027.
Up to S$25 million of sale proceeds will also go towards unit buybacks.
The portfolio underneath looks steady.
Committed occupancy was 96% as at 30 September 2026, and rental reversion for 9M2026 came in at a positive 12%.
Keep a few caveats in mind.
Aggregate leverage stood at 40.5% as at 30 September 2026.
Keppel REIT plans to buy a 51.0% stake in Keppel South Central, a deal with 2.01% pro forma DPU accretion.
The deal comes with income support from
Keppel Ltd
(SGX: BN4) of S$2.23 million a month for up to five years.
New office supply in Singapore also picks up in 2028.
Will Keppel’s special dividend arrive?
Keppel Ltd has not declared a special dividend yet.
The company aims to pay out 10% to 15% of realised proceeds from its asset monetisation programme as special dividends for FY2026.
So far this year, Keppel has completed and realised about S$940 million of asset monetisation.
It targets about S$600 million more by end-2026 from its first six legacy rigs.
Selling assets can fund a one-off payout, but it cannot fund a payout that grows every year.
For that, you need to look at the core business.
Net profit at “the New Keppel” grew more than 20% YoY in 9M2026.
This measure excludes the non-core portfolio for divestment and discontinued operations.
Asset management fees rose 18% to S$354 million over the same period, and recurring income climbed more than 10%.
The wider picture is messier.
Once you include non-core assets, 9M2026 net profit fell 40% YoY, mainly because of impairments and holding costs.
The business update also gave no cash, debt or free cash flow figures.
Until those numbers arrive, you cannot judge how well cash covers the payout.
Get Smart: Price the extra at zero
Before you buy a stock for its
special dividend
, try one simple exercise.
Set the one-off payout to zero and then ask yourself whether the ordinary dividend alone still makes the stock worth owning.
DBS gives you a rising ordinary dividend to answer that question.
Keppel REIT and Keppel will need their next full-year results to give you the same confidence.
If your answer is no, the special dividend is doing too much of the work.

title: Singapore REITs Are Down 8% While the STI Is Up 25% — Should Income Investors Be Worried?
article:
Singapore real estate investment trusts (S-REITs) have fallen 8% while the
Straits Times Index
(SGX: ^STI) has risen 25% since early 2024.
That 33-percentage-point gap leaves income investors asking: has the
real estate
core lost its foundation?
But before assuming S-REITs have hit a brick wall, it is crucial to unpack headline price drops versus total cash returns.
Is the market flagging deeper structural issues, or has the sector simply hit a temporary snag that opens up a prime opportunity?
REITs vs the STI: What Is Driving the Performance Gap?
Looking only at unit price changes misses half the story.
REITs that distribute at least 90% of their taxable income are not taxed on that income at the trust level.
Total returns narrow that 33 percentage-point gap significantly. Still, this marks one of the widest spreads for S-REITs since previous rate-hike cycles.
Record bank profits have fuelled the broader index’s climb, with the STI heavily weighted towards
Singapore banks
such as
DBS Group Holdings Ltd
(SGX: D05).
Conversely, REITs are held for steady income, making their valuations far more sensitive to elevated global
interest rates
than broad market indices.
The silver lining for yield seekers: falling REIT prices automatically boost running distribution yields, provided the underlying DPU (distribution per unit) holds steady.
Why Have Singapore REITs Underperformed?
Debt taken out during the low-interest-rate era must now be refinanced at significantly higher interest rates.
This rising cost of debt chips away at distributable income and places downward pressure on future DPU payouts.
At the same time, income investors no longer need to accept real estate risks to generate cash yields. High-yielding Treasury bills (T-bills), Singapore Savings Bonds, and fixed deposits offer lower-risk competition for income capital.
Furthermore, capital in the markets has aggressively rotated towards high-growth sectors rather than yield-heavy trusts.
Singapore’s banking giants have captured the spotlight by delivering record earnings, pushing REITs out of favour.
Frasers Centrepoint Trust (SGX: J69U), or FCT – The Defensive REIT
FCT serves as the primary income fortress among suburban retail landlords.
Its property portfolio is anchored to non-discretionary necessity spending, essential services, and high-footfall commuter hubs.
In FY2026 (financial year ended 30 September 2026), gross revenue rose 14.2% year-on-year (YoY) to S$444.9 million, driving full-year DPU up 2% to a record high of S$0.1235.
Operational strength remains rock-solid with committed retail occupancy standing at 99.7% and a positive full-year rental reversion rate of 6.6%.
FCT maintains a prudent balance sheet with aggregate leverage at 38.7% and an average full-year borrowing cost of 3.2%.
Its interest coverage ratio (ICR) improved sequentially from 3.66x in June 2026 to 4.37x, providing a healthy financial buffer.
At a recent unit price of S$2.12, FCT offers a distribution yield of 5.8%.
Active asset enhancements at NEX and Causeway Point, paired with debt repayment using White Sands’ divestment proceeds, position FCT for continued cash flow stability.
Keppel DC REIT (SGX: AJBU) – The Growth REIT
Keppel DC REIT provides pure-play exposure to data centres, benefiting directly from global cloud expansion and rapid artificial intelligence adoption.
In the first nine months of 2026 (9M2026), gross revenue climbed 13.3% YoY to S$365.3 million, lifting distributable income by 16.7% to S$228.0 million.
DPU rose 11.7% to S$0.08571.
The REIT’s portfolio performance remains exceptionally strong, backed by a 93.0% occupancy rate and a positive 9M 2026 rental reversion rate of roughly 14%.
Capital management is disciplined, featuring an aggregate leverage ratio of 36.2% and a low average 9M2026 borrowing cost of 2.6%.
ICR sits at a robust 6.5x.
At a recent unit price of S$2.14, the trust delivers an annual dividend yield of 4.66%.
The potential for catalysts is high, supported by sponsor
Keppel Ltd
(SGX: BN4) and the October 2026 acquisition of Tokyo Data Centres 4 and 5 for JPY168.4 billion.
Suntec REIT (SGX: T82U) – The High-Yield Opportunity
Suntec REIT represents a high-yield play for investors willing to evaluate underlying asset value against market headline risks.
Its portfolio includes Suntec City, a stake in Marina Bay Financial Centre, and a collection of properties in Australia and the UK.
In the first half of 2026 (1H2026), distributable income surged 25.5% YoY to S$116.5 million.
DPU jumped 24.8% over the same period to S$0.03936, supported by operational strength across Suntec City Mall and lower financing costs.
In 3Q2026, the REIT declared a quarterly DPU of S$0.02017.
At a current unit price of S$1.37, Suntec REIT trades at a distribution yield of 5.06%.
Strong momentum in Singapore’s office and retail sectors is lifting results, even as overseas assets and rising refinancing costs weigh on sentiment.
For patient investors, ongoing capital management and strong Singapore retail reversions provide potential re-rating upside.
Should Income Investors Be Worried About Falling REIT Prices?
A falling unit price does not mean your income is shrinking.
REIT distributions depend on how much cash the properties bring in, so your DPU can stay steady even if the market punishes the unit price.
However, price weakness can signal coming DPU cuts, higher refinancing costs, or falling property valuations.
The real question to ask: is the real estate business behind the REIT struggling, or are investors just souring on the sector for now?
Get Smart: Don’t Confuse Underperformance With Opportunity
Don’t just chase after beaten-down REITs hoping for a quick bargain.
A 33-percentage-point gap means the market’s shifting, but lower prices on their own don’t mean you’ve found a steal.
The real opportunity lies in tuning out sector noise to isolate resilient REITs with dependable DPU, high occupancy and battle-tested balance sheets.

title: The Mathematics of Compounding: CPF SA Guaranteed Interest vs. Variable Blue-Chip Dividend Growth
article:
Most of us know compounding is powerful.
Fewer of us stop to look at the numbers.
In Singapore, there are two very different ways to put it to work.
On one side, you’ve got your CPF Special Account (SA), quietly doing its thing with guaranteed, government-backed interest.
On the other,
dividend blue chips
, where your money rides on real business earnings, payouts, and market mood swings.
Both grow your wealth, but how they get the job done is night and day.
So which could leave you with more after 10, 20 or 30 years?
How Compounding Works: The Power of Time
Compounding simply means earning returns on your returns.
Your money grows, then that bigger pile grows again, and so on.
For stocks, this only works if you
reinvest your dividends
.
Spend them, and you’re collecting income, not compounding.
And because growth stacks up year after year, even a small gap in returns can snowball into a big difference over decades.
CPF Special Account: The Appeal of Predictable Compounding
Your SA earns at least 4% a year.
The rate is pegged to the 12-month average yield of 10-year Singapore Government Securities plus 1%, but the government guarantees a 4% floor, now extended to 31 December 2027.
That floor is doing real work.
For 4Q2026, the pegged rate remains below 4%, so the floor is what keeps SA savings at 4%.
If you’re below 55, you also earn up to 1% extra on the first S$60,000 of your combined CPF balances.
Members aged 55 and above get an extra 2% on the first first S$30,000 and 1% on the next S$30,000, but this mostly goes into their Retirement Account (RA), as their SA has closed.
So what does 4% do to S$10,000?
Investment Period
CPF Savings at 4%*
10 years

20 years
S$21,911
30 years
S$32,434
*Assumes 4% a year, compounded annually, with no top-ups or withdrawals.
Your money more than triples over 30 years, with zero exposure to market swings.
The trade-off?
It’s locked away.
Unlike shares in a brokerage account, you can’t withdraw it whenever you like.
Blue-Chip Dividend Stocks: The Potential for Higher Returns
With stocks, compounding happens when you reinvest dividends to buy more shares, which then pay you even more dividends.
Even better if the company keeps growing its earnings and payouts.
Singapore’s blue chips have been doing just that.
DBS Group Holdings Ltd
(SGX: D05) posted a record net profit of S$8.82 billion for the first nine months of 2026 (9M2026), up 2.0% year on year (YoY).
The company also declared a quarterly dividend of S$0.81 per share, consisting of S$0.66 ordinary dividend and S$0.15 capital return dividend.
Oversea-Chinese Banking Corporation Limited
(SGX: O39), or OCBC, grew even faster,  with 9M2026 net profit up 10.0% YoY to S$6.24 billion.
Earlier this year, it also raised its interim dividend by 15.0% YoY to S$0.47 per share, paying out 50.0% of its first-half profit.
Singapore Exchange Limited
(SGX: S68) grew adjusted net profit after tax (NPAT) by 24.6% YoY to S$759.5 million in FY2026.
On top of the 4QFY2026 dividend of S$0.115 per share, SGX declared a one-off dividend of S$0.125 per share funded by capital recycling gains, bringing its FY2026 total dividend to S$0.57 per share, up 52.0% YoY.
Excluding the one-off, the dividend rose about 18.7%.
But unlike CPF interest, none of this is guaranteed.
DBS’s third-quarter profit, for one, fell 5% YoY to S$2.81 billion as market trading income slumped 65% amid weaker equity markets.
Share prices swing, and companies can cut dividends when times get tough.
That’s why it pays to focus on total returns, dividends plus price gains, rather than yield alone.
S$10,000 Invested: CPF SA vs. Blue-Chip Stocks Over 30 Years
Here’s how S$10,000 could grow under different return assumptions.

Assumes annual compounding, reinvested dividends and no top-ups. Stock returns are hypothetical total returns.
At 3% a year, stocks actually trail the CPF SA.
At 6%, S$10,000 grows to about S$57,435 after 30 years, about 1.8 times CPF’s S$32,434.
At 8%, it exceeds S$100,000, more than three times CPF.
Notice that moving from 6% to 8% alone adds over S$43,000.
That’s how much small differences matter over time.
Just remember, real stock returns rise and fall along the way, and actual results can look very different.
Which Approach Is Better for Long-Term Investors?
There’s no clear winner, because they do different jobs.
The CPF SA forms a solid retirement base for those who seek stability: predictable growth and protected capital.
The trade-off is limited access to your money.
Blue chips offer growth and flexibility.
You get the potential for higher returns, and you can sell or spend the dividends when you need to.
In exchange, you’ll have to sit through market swings, possible dividend cuts and even losses.
That’s why
combining both
can work well for many investors.
Let CPF be your stable foundation, and let blue chips add income and long-term growth on top.
Just stay diversified and give your investments enough time.

title: Top 3 Temasek-Backed Blue Chips Beating the Market YTD
article:

Three Temasek-linked blue chips did even better.

All three figures include dividends and cover the first 10 months of 2026.
Temasek, a global investment company headquartered in Singapore, owned 28% of DBS and 51% of ST Engineering as at 31 March 2026.
Its link to SGX is less direct: Temasek owns SEL Holdings, which held a 23.35% stake in SGX as at 1 September 2026.

Can DBS keep growing as its trading income slumps?
The customer business is still growing.
The trading desk is another matter.

The 3Q2026 results, released on 5 November 2026, look different.

Here’s the thing: markets trading non-interest income fell to S$17 million from S$419 million.

title: Prabowo said to accept Indonesia vice president resignation
article:
Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto has accepted the resignation of Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka, according to people with knowledge of the matter.

Gibran handed over his resignation letter in a meeting between the two men late Wednesday, the people said, speaking anonymously about a private conversation.

Gibran, the son of former President Joko Widodo, had faced growing calls from politicians for his impeachment over questions about his educational credentials. He had been accused of failing to prove that he met a high school-equivalent education requirement to run for vice president in the 2024 election, despite holding a university degree.

The Government Communication Agency didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment outside of regular office hours. A representative for the vice president also didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.

Budi Arie Setiadi, head of the pro-Widodo volunteer group Projo, separately confirmed that Gibran had submitted his resignation.

It wasn’t immediately clear when Gibran’s resignation would take effect, or whether the People’s Consultative Assembly had been formally notified. The constitution provides a separate process for filling a vacancy in the vice presidency.

See also: Thailand EV tax gets carmakers weighing more local production

The resignation comes a day after Gibran met with Prabowo for more than two hours, after which the vice president said he planned to seek to validate certain documents through the courts to address allegations against him.

Gibran’s mooted exit could reshape the political alliance that helped Prabowo win power. It also likely marks a significant turning point in relations between Prabowo and Widodo, widely known as Jokowi. The two former rivals formed an alliance ahead of the 2024 presidential election, with Gibran’s selection as Prabowo’s running mate cementing their partnership.

Jokowi was pivotal in helping Prabowo secure victory after two unsuccessful presidential bids. Their alliance gave Prabowo access to Widodo’s political network and public support while ensuring that Jokowi’s eldest son entered one of the country’s highest political offices.

See also: Singapore, Johor and Riau Islands triangle is ‘strategic insurance’, says energy expert

The political upheaval also comes amid wider discontent with the government. Student and civil society groups staged demonstrations in several Indonesian cities this week over economic conditions, environmental policies and civil liberties.

In Yogyakarta, on the island of Java, police detained 154 people after clashes erupted near the provincial legislature Tuesday night. Authorities said a group attacked a building with fireworks, Molotov cocktails and stones, while a local legal aid organization alleged excessive police force. Police said they were investigating the violence.

News of Gibran’s imminent departure came just hours after 120 lawmakers from all eight parliamentary factions, including 11 members of Prabowo’s own Gerindra party, submitted a motion that could lead to Gibran’s impeachment. The House had been preparing to take up the proposal at a plenary session Thursday.

Gibran had already expressed his intention to resign during a meeting with Prabowo on Tuesday, according to State Secretary Prasetyo Hadi. Prasetyo said the president hadn’t rejected the proposal but had offered advice.

Speaking afterward, Gibran said Prabowo had encouraged him to continue fighting to prove the validity of his academic records through the courts. That account was disputed by government communications chief Syahganda Nainggolan, while Coordinating Law Minister Yusril Ihza Mahendra said the court rulings were final and left no avenue for Gibran’s proposed legal challenge.

The Supreme Court last month invalidated a government certificate issued in 2019 to establish the equivalence of Gibran’s overseas education to an Indonesian high-school qualification.

In its full judgment published this week, the court said the supporting documents failed to establish that Gibran had completed the required level of education and ordered authorities to revoke the certificate.

The ruling renewed questions about whether Gibran met the educational requirements to contest the 2024 election. It didn’t automatically remove him from office, leaving the question of his departure to a separate constitutional process.

The timing of Gibran’s departure remains significant because the constitution requires the People’s Consultative Assembly, also known as MPR, to choose a new vice president within 60 days of a vacancy, from two candidates nominated by Prabowo.

That process gives Prabowo a pivotal role in selecting a new deputy, with implications for the balance of power among the political parties supporting his government.

Yusril said Tuesday that a voluntary resignation would require a formal written statement to the MPR, which would establish the vacancy and request two candidates from the president.

It remains unclear whether lawmakers will proceed with the planned consideration of the impeachment motion Thursday following Gibran’s submission of his resignation.

title: Nvidia’s bull case hinges on CEO Huang surviving China spy probe
article:
(Nov 11): Nvidia Corp’s investigation of chief executive officer Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy is raising questions about the company’s future and sending its stock into a tailspin.

In the wake of Huang’s shocking disclosure in a memo to Nvidia employees on Sunday, Wall Street is wondering if the biggest and most important artificial intelligence (AI) chipmaker will be able to keep its leader and public face. The stock fell roughly 10% in the two sessions since the news hit, making it the second-worst performer in the S&P 500 Index over that time, and it closed at its lowest since March 30 on Tuesday. The shares jumped about 3% at the open on Wednesday as the stock market broadly rallied.

Now, cracks are emerging in Wall Street’s overwhelmingly bullish sentiment towards the AI darling. Baird downgraded the stock to neutral on Wednesday, while Morgan Stanley removed it as a Top Pick. Both cited growing uncertainty surrounding Huang.

“If he goes, the bull case goes with him,” said Jay Goldberg of Seaport Global Securities, the only analyst with a sell rating on the stock. “Trying to conceive of an Nvidia without Jensen seems impossible. If he gets ousted, the floor would fall out from under the stock. I don’t know how likely that is, but it would be shattering.”

Nvidia shares had been under pressure prior to this crisis as investors increasingly questioned the durability of the AI trade and the hundreds of billions of dollars in capital expenditures that are funding it. The stock got hammered after the midterm elections delivered a rebuke to building AI data centres and is on pace for its sixth-straight week in the red, something that hasn’t happened since 2012. Nvidia shares have fallen more than 20% since hitting a high on Oct 6, bringing the company’s market value down to around US$4 trillion from US$5.8 trillion a month ago.

See also: Wall Street bonuses seen climbing before prospects weaken

“Even before the midterms, the market was changing how it felt about the cost of the AI buildout, and the election only increased the level of uncertainty,” said Simeon Wallis, chief investment officer of Aprio Wealth Management. “Now it has to wait and see what happens with Nvidia’s board, which adds more fog around the story.”

This earnings season showed how concerned investors are about AI spending, especially at companies that are posting negative free cash flow like Alphabet Inc, Meta Platforms Inc and Amazon.com Inc. Those three represent about 23% of Nvidia’s revenue, according to supply chain data compiled by Bloomberg, and their stocks all slumped after their latest earnings reports showed rising capital expenditures for AI.

The prospect that these so-called hyperscalers could pull back on their spending gained new potency following last week’s election victories by candidates who oppose data centres in key states like Texas. If it becomes harder to build AI infrastructure, Nvidia’s growth outlook will invariably suffer.

See also: IBM to end immigration sponsorship for roles in biggest unit

“It’s too early to tell whether things have fundamentally changed,” Wallis said. “But it’s hard to have much conviction over the short term.”

Of course, one upside to the selloff for investors is it has made Nvidia’s stock price historically cheap. The shares are trading around 12 times earnings expected over the next 12 months, their lowest multiple since 2013. Measured as a ratio, Nvidia hasn’t been this inexpensive relative to the S&P 500 since 2002. And its PEG ratio, which is calculated by dividing its price-to-earnings ratio by its profit growth rate, stands at an all-time low of 0.162.

“The uncertainty around Jensen is such a large, looming problem that it is now very difficult to suss out what a fair value would be,” Seaport’s Goldberg said. “It is easy to see it getting worse before it gets better.”

So far, analysts have held their estimates for Nvidia’s earnings and revenue in fiscal 2027 and 2028. However, they’re likely to be refreshed next week after the company posts its third-quarter results on Nov 17. The chipmaker’s net income and revenue are expected to jump more than 90% in the quarter and fiscal year, which ends on Jan 31.

That soaring growth and the stock’s low multiple are the key reasons Wall Street remains largely positive on Nvidia. Of the 82 analysts tracked by Bloomberg who follow the stock, 77 have buy ratings, and the average analyst price target indicates expectations that the shares will rise nearly 90% over the next 12 months.

Nvidia’s pricing power and dominance across the AI supply chain, along with it’s healthy profitability, should make the stock appealing to some investors at its current level, according to Daniel Newman, chief executive officer of the Futurum Group. The catch, of course, is the extreme degree of uncertainty surrounding the company.

“The optimistic view is that this is limited to a personal indiscretion, and if the investigation clears him of any additional wrongdoing, the stock should recover,” he said. “The problem is we don’t know, and this is a unique and wild situation. I’m constructive on AI, but I’m watching Nvidia. I think a lot of investors feel the same — the selloff has created a lot of opportunities, but until this uncertainty plays out, they might pick something else besides Nvidia.”

title: Mercedes CEO flags pivot to strategy of ‘100% China for China’
article:
(Nov 11): Mercedes-Benz Group AG’s struggles with shrinking demand in China mean it’s being forced into a complete overhaul of its business in the world’s biggest auto market, according to chief executive officer Ola Källenius.

A previously successful hybrid model under which Mercedes split production between regional sites before assembling the finished vehicle in China for the local market no longer works, Källenius said on Wednesday at a Sueddeutsche Zeitung newspaper forum in Berlin.

Alongside a broader push to cut costs and lift productivity, the German manufacturer is now pursuing a “100% China for China” strategy, with the new electric Mercedes E-Class set to be the first model produced there in the second half of next year, he added.

Mercedes is in the midst of one of its biggest product and cost overhauls in years as the Stuttgart-based automaker tries to restore profitability. The company has been focusing on selling fewer but more expensive cars, relying on higher-end models to support margins.

In China, once a major source of profit, that strategy has come under increasing pressure. Mercedes sales in the country slumped 31% in the third quarter due to weaker luxury demand and stiffer competition from more sophisticated local rivals.

“We, and anyone else who wants to be a global player, will have to adapt the entire business system, because a competitive fight is taking place in China among more than 100 brands,” Källenius said.

See also: VW scraps advanced factory plan as earnings squeeze deepens

China remains central to Mercedes’ turnaround plans and it would be a mistake to try to pull back from the Asian nation, even as consumers there remain “very, very cautious”, Källenius said.

“The auto industry is perhaps the most interconnected in the world,” he told SZ forum delegates. “It would be completely illusory to think you can break that apart so we have to cooperate intelligently.”

Mercedes’ reset is creating tensions in Germany, where it says production is no longer competitive compared to sites it operates in Eastern Europe and the US.

See also: Volkswagen EV sales in China climb to monthly record in sign of turnaround

Management has pushed for longer working hours without additional pay and other savings, warning that further measures may be needed if current efforts fall short.

Mercedes has indicated the additional savings could be equivalent to the cost of closing two plants, though it stressed the comparison was illustrative and no specific sites have been identified for shuttering.

Källenius said if you created a cost index with Germany at 100, the US would be at around 80 and Mercedes needs to bring its domestic cost burden down to that level.

“We can’t hide anymore,” he said, warning that ongoing talks with labour officials on extending working hours must produce tangible results. “If we are not ready to take a significant leap, then we will have clearly less industrial activity in this country in 10 years time.”

title: US mortgage rates fall for fourth week, lifting home purchases
article:
(Nov 11): US mortgage rates declined for a fourth straight week, boosting home-purchase applications by the most since mid-April and giving a tiny spark to the deflated housing market.

 

The contract rate on a 30-year fixed mortgage fell nine basis points to 7.21% in the week ended Nov 6, according to data released on Wednesday by the Mortgage Bankers Association. Borrowing costs have fallen nearly 30 basis points from an almost two-year high of 7.5% early last month, although they remain prohibitively high for many Americans.

A gauge of loan applications for home purchases jumped 7.5%, marking just the second weekly increase since the end of August. The group’s refinance index rose 4.5%. The measure, which has advanced three straight weeks, is still near the lowest level since January 2025.

While the drop in rates is welcome news for the housing market, it may take a sustained decline to motivate potential buyers. Contract signings on previously owned homes dropped to a record low in September following a rapid run-up in mortgage rates during the month.

On Thursday, the National Association of Realtors will release figures on existing-home closings in October. The median forecast in a Bloomberg survey of economists calls for a decline to the lowest level since 2010.

title: VW scraps advanced factory plan as earnings squeeze deepens
article:
(Nov 11): Volkswagen AG is scrapping a major advanced-manufacturing project at its sprawling headquarter as falling profits force Europe’s biggest carmaker to rethink investment across its German factories.

Volkswagen won’t implement its so-called Gamechanger manufacturing concept “in the form previously planned” in Wolfsburg because of the company’s strained finances, it said on Wednesday. Work will continue on its next-generation electric platform and models including the ID. Roc, a planned electric sport utility vehicle.

The retreat shows how quickly Volkswagen’s financial squeeze is spilling into long-term investment decisions. Earnings have deteriorated across the group, with China turning from a major profit engine into a drag and management now pushing for about EUR31 billion (US$34.52 billion or $44.22 billion) in savings while still funding new electric cars, software and factories.

The new technology was intended to introduce new manufacturing techniques at Wolfsburg that could later be deployed more widely across the group.

Among them was so-called gigacasting, which uses enormous presses to make large sections of a vehicle body in fewer pieces, reducing the number of components and manufacturing steps. Tesla Inc. helped pioneer the method in modern car production and uses large aluminum casting machines at its Grünheide factory near Berlin.

Volkswagen’s powerful works council chief Daniela Cavallo called the decision a ‘flagrant breach’ of a December 2024 agreement and accused the company of giving up its ambition to lead in manufacturing technology.

See also: Volkswagen EV sales in China climb to monthly record in sign of turnaround

Cavallo added labour would resist moving production of the combustion-engine Golf from Wolfsburg to Mexico until Volkswagen explains what the change means for jobs and factory volumes.

Production of the top-selling model is due to move to Mexico next year to make room for future electric models, under a plan labour representatives agreed to in the 2024 pact.

Under Germany’s system of co-determination, worker representatives hold half the seats on Volkswagen’s supervisory board and wield significant influence over major restructuring decisions.

See also: Audi and Mercedes hit by walkouts in union push for higher wages

The dispute adds another complication to Volkswagen’s effort to shrink its high-cost German operations. Volkswagen is targeting roughly 100,000 job cuts worldwide as it shrinks capacity and lowers costs, with its retrenchment now reaching deep into Germany.

The carmaker has also raised the prospect of closing German factories, a step it has avoided throughout the postwar era.

title: Sats reports 2QFY2027 earnings of $81.1 mil, up 2.8% y-o-y
article:
Sats has reported earnings of $81.1 million for its 2QFY2027 ended Sept, up 2.8% y-o-y. Revenue in the same quarter ended Sept was $1.71 billion, up 9% y-o-y, lifted by higher cargo and meal volumes.

Kerry Mok, the company's president and CEO calls the 2QFY2027 numbers an indication of the strength of the comapny's diversified global network and resilience of the business model.
